paragraphs: The bus left me at the edge of a town I could barely [[locate]] on the map, with [[mist]] on the hills and a [[path]] down to the [[shore]]. I had come from [[China]] to translate a [[Spanish]] novel, and the house I had rented belonged to a [[housewife]] who welcomed me with the [[informality]] of an old friend. She showed me to a [[cubicle]] under the stairs, with a [[shelf]], a [[pretty]] window on the yard, and a [[low]] bed that creaked. The room was [[remote]] from the town's noise, and for the first time in months I felt I could [[relax]]. [[Despite]] the dust, the [[area]] beyond the last street was [[alive]] with [[flowers|flower]]. A farmer was [[shearing|shear]] a sheep beside the cottage I had [[borrowed|borrow]] for the summer.

In the morning I walked to the [[archaeological]] dig above the bay, where a team was uncovering a [[century]]-old fishing village. A [[guard]] at the gate checked my name, handed me a first-[[aid]] kit, and pointed to a [[circle]] of stones that had once been a hearth. The grant had [[enabled|enable]] the dig to continue, and a [[model]] of the old village stood in the site hut. Under the soil I found a [[lump]] of rusted iron and a [[chunk]] of [[shell]] that the [[tools|tool]] had cut cleanly. My camera [[lens]] could [[detect]] markings no eye could see, and the bay itself was [[inhabited|inhabit]] by a small, rare fish. Every [[object]] had to be [[logged|log]] before it was moved. The dig was a [[branch]] of a larger project, and we had to [[traverse]] a narrow path to reach it each morning.

That afternoon I visited the [[laboratory]] where a friend was studying a [[hybrid]] fish and its [[chromosomes|chromosome]]. She explained how [[toxic]] algae could [[infest]] a bay and how the [[frequency]] of blooms had risen [[sharply|sharp]]. Her team tried to [[isolate]] the cause with [[maximal]] care and almost no money. Their [[focus]] was a [[flaw]] in the [[design]] of the sampling net, which let small fish escape and made every count unreliable. Standing there, I felt the [[urge]] to [[write]] everything down, and my [[brain]] began to [[shape]] a chapter.

On Saturday the beach [[alarm]] rang twice, and a [[shark]] was seen beyond the buoys. The reaction was close to [[hysteria]]: people screamed, a woman dropped her towel, and two boys [[floated|float]] [[recklessly]] on a raft, unaware. A [[brave]] lifeguard paddled out with a [[lure]] and turned the fish away from the [[shore]]. Sharks rarely [[prey]] on people, but fear does not need [[logic]]. We were told to stay in shallow water, and the crowd slowly calmed down.

On Sunday I went into the old [[church]] on the hill, not out of [[religion]] but out of curiosity, and looked up at the carved [[Christ]] above the door. The sermon was about [[shame]] and [[guilt]], and the priest said that no one was [[unworthy]] of [[esteem]]. I thought of the [[ideology]] behind such words, and of the [[utopia]] that every generation builds and loses. A woman near me began to [[moan]] softly, and someone helped her outside. The [[modern]] world [[misunderstands|misunderstand]] such places, I thought, and [[derides|deride]] what it cannot [[use]].

My landlady's daughter had a new [[infant]], [[born]] three weeks early, and the whole street took turns holding him. His [[hunger]] was enormous; he cried until his face turned red, then fed and slept. His first [[tooth]] had not come, and his grandmother, [[infirm]] and slow, sang to him in a dialect I could not follow. She said that in her day a housewife had no time to be tired, and that [[love]] was mostly work. I held him for an hour, and for once I [[felt|feel]] no [[hurry]].

The town's [[president]] had called a meeting about the new road [[toll]], and the debate turned into a [[battle]]. A group of [[motorists|motorist]] in a [[chrome]]-trimmed car threatened a [[boycott]] of the ferry company. They said the [[levy]] would fall on locals, [[because]] tourists never paid it. Older residents said the [[dearth]] of parking was the real [[downside]], and that the council should [[maintain]] the [[guidelines|guideline]] it had published. The argument drifted to [[Brexit]] and [[sanctions|sanction]], then to [[trade]], and [[therefore]] to everything else. Someone joked about [[espionage]], and the [[inhuman]] speed of the vote made the joke feel true. No one was [[allowed|allow]] to speak for more than two minutes, [[despite]] the heat, and the [[dirty]] little [[misuse]] of a public [[task]] was plain to all.

That night a [[chill]] came off the water, and clouds began to [[loom]] over the bay. We took [[shelter]] in a house she had [[inherited|inherit]] from her mother, and the storm [[broke|break]] with a noise like a [[ship]] hitting the dock. Water [[flowed|flow]] down the hill and [[escaped|escape]] through a broken drain. The [[alarm]] rang again, but this time it was only the wind. By midnight the sky was clear, and the [[mist]] had lifted.

On Monday a fisherman was brought in with a deep [[wound]] in his arm, [[hurt]] by a [[tractor]] chain and [[unshaven|shave]] for days. The doctor on the night [[shift]] was young but careful, and he found an [[error]] in the first [[definition]] of the injury. There were rumours of [[malpractice]] at another clinic, where a [[low-level]] nurse had been left alone with [[infirm]] patients, and a mask was their only [[shield]]. The [[toll]] of such stories [[accrues|accrue]] slowly, and people [[remember]] them long after the official report is forgotten.

The village festival began with a [[tour]] of the old quarter and ended with a speech that [[bored|bore]] even the mayor. A [[flight]] from Madrid had brought a [[Spanish]] [[airline's|airline]] crew, and a dancer in a [[wasp-waist]] dress sold [[cigars|cigar]]. The [[townsfolk]] [[mocked|mock]] the visitors gently, and the visitors [[mocked|mock]] the [[folk]] music back. It was the [[anniversary]] of the [[iconic]] lighthouse, and someone read a [[brief]] [[essay]] about its first keeper. The [[guest]] of honour was a [[novelist]] whose [[Polynesian]] saga I had been translating all summer.

I had been translating her novel for two years, and her [[catchword]] for the book was 'the sea remembers'. She was a [[millennial]] with a [[clear-eyed]] view of history, and she distrusted every [[pretty]] phrase. We argued about a single word for an hour, and I [[began|begin]] to see translation as a [[mode]] of reading. Her prose was [[mixed]] with island words, a [[hybrid]] language that no dictionary could capture.

By August I had begun to [[rely]] on the town's slow mornings, and to [[owe]] the landlady more than rent. We [[shared|share]] bread, tools and [[guesswork]], and she never made me feel like a [[guest]]. She said a good life was not about [[lucre]] but about [[choosing|choose]] what to [[aim]] at. I was not sure I was [[equal]] to that, but I was willing to [[bother]] trying. The [[best]] I could do was write honestly, and [[worse]] still was to pretend I understood more than I did. [[Ahead]] lay a [[century]] of such small decisions, each one [[shaping|shape]] the shore. The town had been [[remolded|remold]] (or [[remoulded|remould]]) by three summers of visitors, and it would be remade again.

One afternoon I got lost on the hill, and a [[guide]] led me down, [[upright]] and patient, with a [[fly]] circling his hat. I had [[misplaced|misplace]] my map and wasted an hour in [[vain]], which taught me to [[own]] my [[mistake]]. A [[misleading|mislead]] sign at the [[top]] of the path pointed nowhere, and at the [[bottom]] a [[loop]] of road led back to the start. I began to [[use]] my phone as a [[tool]] and to [[alert]] the others when I moved. The sea was so clear that I could [[touch]] the bottom, and I did not want to [[lose]] my way again.

A [[flu]] went through the town in the last week of August, and half the [[townsfolk]] stayed in bed. I cooked for the landlady: I would [[chop]] vegetables, boil rice, and [[detach]] the leaves from the herbs. We avoided the [[shellfish|shell]] from the north bank, which had been [[toxic]] since June, and drank tea whose [[flavor]] (or [[flavour]]) came from wild mint. The kitchen was [[dirty]] by city standards, but on the last Sunday I [[folded|fold]] dough for bread while she watched.

On my last evening we sat on the wall and watched a [[ship]] move [[toward]] the harbour mouth, and later, walking home, I kept turning [[towards]] the water. The town and I had changed, [[alike]] in small ways, and [[despite]] the difference in our ages we had become friends. She [[reminded|remind]] me to [[remember]] the small things, and to write them down before they [[deteriorated|deteriorate]]. I promised to send her the finished book, and she said she would [[write]] back in her [[upright]] hand. I had come to translate a novel and was leaving with something more [[insidious]]: the sense that the town had translated me.
